basis: Published node definitions, bound metric names, units, transformations and failure rules; source-backed consequence models must still be reviewed separately.
decisions: A global temperature anomaly describes climate state. An impact model must attribute health, service and ecological consequences; degrees are not harm units.
Source-resolved methane mass needs atmospheric lifetime, forcing and consequence models. Annual emissions are different from atmospheric concentration and cumulative harm.
Forest conversion is a pressure with direct habitat effects. Annual gross hectares are not the current attributable condition stock or a supported human consequence total.
Agricultural input intensity requires source-specific pathways to pollution, habitat and health losses. Food-production benefits are not a damage amount.
Commodity demand is an activity measure. It requires attributable land, water and production impacts and cannot be read as hunger or harm.
Built-up expansion is a land-use pressure. Population share and added hectares alone do not establish net heat, flooding, health or habitat consequences.
The bound material footprint and consumption series measure pressure, not remaining resources or their depletion. A resource-specific stock and consequence model is missing.
The bound inventory covers fossil and industrial CO2. Land-use emissions mentioned in the definition need a separate inventory; climate consequences require source allocation.
Threshold hours at a grid point measure humid-heat exposure. Population exposure, activity and health response are needed to establish harm.
Daily precipitation anomalies require flood, exposure and consequence models. Rain intensity alone is not realized damage.
High-altitude aerosol mass requires transport, atmospheric effects and receptor-specific consequence models. It is not ground-level inhaled dose.
Well-level departures require aquifer coverage and attributable service and ecosystem effects. A local datum departure is not a global burden.
Heat-attributable deaths are a health endpoint, but a DALY route needs source-supported years lost and morbidity coverage. Do not add the overlapping heatwave mortality node.
An age-standardized mortality rate cannot be multiplied by a raw population to obtain an actual death total. A separate source-native joint DALY endpoint is available with its own boundary.
Root-zone percentiles and duration describe a water deficit. Plant condition and attributable human consequences need separate endpoints.
SPI drought duration describes sustained dryness, not the population or ecosystem loss it causes. Consequences need a matched causal comparison.
Tree-cover loss in a water-supply watershed requires forest-condition, water-treatment and service effects. Hectares alone are not those consequences.
Generation shortfall is an intermediate service outcome. Replacement power and served populations determine whether essential functions were actually lost.
Production share describes dependence. Supported energy, brine and actual supply-interruption pathways are needed; reliance itself is not realized harm.
The bound ice indicators do not by themselves measure full season length, animal condition or affected travel services. Each needs a bounded consequence route.
A tropical Atlantic temperature index needs location-specific rainfall and impact pathways. Neither phase has a universal harmful sign.
The share of assessed stocks outside sustainable levels is not area-weighted condition loss or the prevalence of collapse. Stock coverage and actual consequences must be resolved.
Landing shortfalls require catch, substitution and trade attribution before assigning food or livelihood losses. A tonne is not a loss-of-function year.
Gas-generation share is a dependency and activity indicator. Direct plant-health models cover only part of this broader node and cannot supply its whole score.
Cooling withdrawals must distinguish consumption, return flows and competing uses. Water volumes alone do not establish service or ecological damage.
The bound GBIF occurrence coverage is not an intactness estimate. Abundance, reference communities, sampling effort, area and attribution are required before condition loss can be calculated.
Connectivity shares describe one ecological characteristic. A fixed ecosystem profile and spatially resolved attributable loss are needed; the percentage is not a full-condition deficit.
Mangrove extent and buffer width describe habitat structure. Protection and human-loss effects require local hydrodynamic and exposure models; habitat condition needs its own profile.
The bound survey describes U.S. river and stream community condition. It cannot establish global collapse, lake condition, or a complete six-class ecosystem profile.
Trap biomass trends require sampling and area coverage, reference condition and attribution. They are one biological feature, not total ecosystem-condition loss.
Organic-carbon stock is a soil feature and does not uniquely measure humus or all soil functions. Depth, reference states, area and attribution must be fixed.
The bound modeled food-loss endpoint is different from a probability of equipment failure. Nutrition and livelihood consequences need substitution, affected people and function-loss evidence.
Erosion mass is a soil pressure. Remaining soil condition, productivity, downstream effects and attribution are needed; historical removed tonnes cannot be multiplied into a current stock.
Unfrozen-zone area, thickness and duration require hydrological, emissions and ecological pathways. Thaw is not automatically a uniform harmful condition deficit.
Thermal event-days and exposed ocean area require species and ecosystem response models. Exposure area is not damaged area.
Soil density or infiltration relative to a control can support a physical condition feature, but full attributable condition and human consequences remain separate.
Ice-shelf melt and discharge need shelf-specific causal links to land-ice change, sea level and terminal consequences. Global sea-level harm cannot simply be copied.
Disconnected network shares measure structure. They do not establish species persistence, habitat quality or an area-weighted complete condition deficit.
Occupied-cell expansion identifies spread, not harmful invasion or abundance. Impact attribution and source-specific ecological and human endpoints are needed.
Sea-level change requires local relative level, exposure, protection and impact models. Millimetres do not directly measure flooding or harm.
Microbial biomass, activity and diversity must remain distinct features. A source-specific reference, ecosystem area and causal comparison are required.
Monitoring-well trends are not household well failure or the population losing supply. Aquifer weighting, access and service consequences need separate evidence.
Condition-class hectares may support a peatland profile after references and attribution are defined. Drainage status alone cannot supply all condition classes or human effects.
Measured interaction and downstream responses may support ecological features. A single declining taxon does not establish a cascade or its total extent and condition loss.
Vessel delay is an intermediate service outcome. Cargo substitution, essential goods and actual affected functions are needed; delay-hours are not human loss-years.
Nonrenewal is an observed access outcome. It does not directly quantify household function loss, and risk reassessment is not proof of climate attribution.
Deposition is receptor-level pressure. Buffering, chemical change and biological response determine consequences; precursor emissions cannot replace deposited flux.
Declared restrictions need actual lost access and affected person-time. Conservation benefits and avoided shortages must stay distinct from imposed hardship.
The bound annual heat-attributable mortality endpoint overlaps the heat-related mortality node. Event-specific excess mortality needs a separate comparison and cannot be assumed from the title.
Corridor avalanche counts and closure-hours require casualties and actual service-loss evidence. Closures can prevent harm and are not automatically harm-years.
Ice velocity and bearing require route, vessel and ecosystem consequence models. Faster drift has no universal harmful sign.
Soot and albedo changes require source attribution and melt or ecological impact pathways. Local samples cannot establish global harm.
Sediment concentration and flux require habitat, intake and storage consequences. Turbidity or meltwater cannot substitute for source-bound sediment flux.
Hole area and depth require supported albedo, melt and terminal impact pathways. A changed surface feature is not a consequence total.
Persistent woody-cover change requires an ecosystem-specific reference. Low tree cover can be natural savanna condition, so forests' degraded references must not be transferred.
Pigment and albedo can describe natural biological and energy processes. Harm needs a bounded pathway and cannot be assumed from increased pigment biomass.
CAPE and CIN require observed or modeled storm initiation and consequences. Instability alone cannot establish storms or harm.
Habitat area and connectivity require suitability, taxa, reference condition and attribution. Occurrence-source coverage does not itself establish habitat shrinkage.
Site sediment pulses require receptor-specific benthic, water-quality or service endpoints. Glacier retreat cannot by itself establish sediment or ecological harm.
Asset temperature and loading require a validated failure model and actual service consequences. Stress, failure probability and realized outages are different outcomes.
Fracture displacement requires rockfall and exposed-asset models before consequences can be assigned. Freeze-thaw cycles alone do not establish collapse.
Shrub change can involve gains and losses across different ecological features. A habitat-specific counterfactual is needed before assigning a harmful sign.
Taxon-specific density, survival and recruitment can support biological condition features. Source area, detection, reference and cause must be established before aggregation.
Cohort survival and recruitment are biological endpoints. Experimental controls and local arrays cannot be scaled to current global condition without coverage and a causal model.
Forest-cover contraction needs persistent, species- and elevation-specific condition loss. Upper expansion and lower contraction must remain separate.
FIES is a reported access outcome, not biological undernutrition or DALYs. A supported non-health function profile and separate health-overlap review are needed.
The node is an infrastructure pressure while its bound metric describes long-river connectivity. Species passability, ecological condition and human benefits and losses need separate pathways.
Non-revenue water mixes leaks, meter error and authorized unbilled use. Separate real losses before linking water volumes or financial amounts to terminal consequences.
Wildfire-attributed concentration is exposure, not a health outcome. Use source-specific exposure-response and population data while avoiding overlap with aggregate air-pollution burden.
